It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns the original
run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that decli
ned\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carr
ies\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the
third case: the runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two

environments can
 resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

>

[!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back
; the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally car
ry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.\n\n**Swarms, insights**: what a run revealed. Read these in order of cos
t: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry\naggregates them, and swarm run insights run a

model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rate
s, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |
\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismi
ss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insigh
ts` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request the

m. `202`; scheduled, not done |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two ar

ithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, n

ever by the session total.** Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75%, not
 7.5%.
*
**`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a\n regression, and folding the two together makes one look

like the other.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle:
`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismis
sed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismissed, and hidi

ng one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits**; the model c
ost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run
and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting; `force: tr

ue` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (w
ait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), an

d a `403` means
> the feature is not available to your organization; waiting will never help.

**User testing** (`/projects/{pr
ojectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`): publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey
did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once

it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent: r
epublishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environment
Id}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH ...
/studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row
per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's tran
script, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous
visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.**
No body; the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on
an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, en
ding their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project

|

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from granting NE
W access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotati
on\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks, and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you di

d not intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, t
ightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n>

stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite; a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
>

Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing,
what visitors did**: the analytics reads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\

ndeterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId
}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET
.../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rat
e |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window, and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GE
T .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/
windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST
.../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the
window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowI
d` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it s

tays dismissed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usa
ge` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` descr
ibe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `s
taleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map indep
endently. Reading this response never starts analysis.\n\nTaxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme
ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is uncha
nged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version
provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.\n\nCheck `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a\
nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed
